reviews.text: After about six of the many demo months that replaced Reality Break's originally planned early access period, every single post and thread I had made in the Steam forum was suddenly deleted, and I was banned for a month to keep me quiet about it. They also asserted general authority over sites outside Steam, calling talking [i]outside Steam[/i] "subverting" the Steam ban, and grounds for escalation. Such scorched-earth deletion is an unforgivable act. Many hours spent on posts, suggestions, feedback, player help, question answering, etc., that the dev themselves as well as others expressed appreciation for... All typical, normal stuff, like anyone would expect to find in the forum, all just gone one day on someone's whim. Now, only a few scattered quotes in others' posts remain. Doing something so extreme and [i]without even a hint of warning[/i] was absolutely repulsive, and I've seen other complaints about removing posts here. A potential customer should keep this in mind, and I have to recommend against engaging, despite the dev's lip service to respect and the principle of charity. Supporting the abusive and ugly projections I received through their moderation messages certainly is not what I consider "charitable". And, threatening to punish you for speaking in [i]other[/i] sites beyond their forum, as though their control and censure should extend everywhere, defies rationality and should never be countenanced. Naturally, I stay banned in [i]this[/i] forum, because I will not be told where I am [i]allowed[/i] to speak by some random game. Neither should anyone else. Making a cool game is supposed to be the hard part. Don't screw up the community side so badly. And hey, maybe if community/playtesting priorities were in a better place, the game wouldn't have released in a state that would make most early access games blush--riddled with bugs, unignorable math errors, easily triggered progression breaks, missing key drops, people losing saves (because why bother to just save safely, right?), and an impenetrableness that leaves core feature unlock achievement stats still around 10% even with pretty high activity (more people have [i]finished the game[/i] than unlocked even one subclass). Was no one left who would voice these problems before launch customers crash into them, or were they just too busy patting the dev on the back to bother? Hopefully we'll be leaving this early access phase before too many weeks (edit: [i]months[/i]...) go by, now that problems are harder to just ignore than noisy community members. Hopefully.
从demo的时候就关注的游戏，太空射击题材的轻度肉鸽游戏，创意和玩法都很棒，就是这个UI界面看久了有点光污染费眼睛

类暗黑玩法就是无敌好玩！ 太空背景的类暗黑，有自己的特殊机制，部分装备可以消耗稀有资源升级词条属性甚至稀有度。同时还在装备取舍上做了些创新，因为是太空背景，各类武器也都是枪弹炮、导弹激光啥的，除了考虑武器的稀有度和数值外，武器的使用顺不顺手也是取舍的一个重要考量。 重置世界的轮回设计有点像暗黑里面的不同难度世界，局外成长自然就是巅峰点数了[strike] 光是想想都肝痒痒，不说了继续肝游戏了 [/strike]

Calculations of dmg taken by touching an enemy or asteroid is just bad. I can have high enough armor to tank an enemies shots but if I run into them or asteroid then I take a percent based dmg to my hp. Fix this cause its just bad gameplay.

Don't really understand the appeal. Everything I've done in this game has been the same, fly around and shoot stuff without any real change in mechanics/gameplay. You're just a stat stick and skill level doesn't really do much to enhance gameplay. The "rewrite system" isn't very inspiring either. It's neat that you can change an item, but you're only given predetermined stats to pick from, so it's not like you're really making anything unique. I'd much rather just be able to craft something to my liking completely or even craft random stats like POE2, you at least have more reason to grind that way. Game has a few good ideas, but the few it has are just detrimental to the ARPG style IMO.
我第一次接触这个题材的有戏，试用版非常合我胃口，期待了很久。肉鸽但装备有自己的参与度。这非常好。但我感觉可以改变一些设置，血量不显示在飞机上。初期血量低很容易突然阵亡。可以简化一个小血条，在少于一半或三分之一有显示。有助于新手初体验。总之满分100，作者应得95分。期待作者将来的游戏！

记事本写个BAT脚本(文件后缀记得改.bat)双击执行修改系统时间,这样方便"分析",再也不用等N多个二三十分钟了哈哈哈("钱"和"改写点"都是双浮点类型CE自己改就行)即便改了这些想要刷NB"词条"都要很久.... 吐槽下:这游戏做装备太难了,还非常鸡肋完全是给"现实点"升级全都点满的后期玩家准备的功能,要先刷到附带NB"词条"的装备,然后拆解获得NB"词条"假设是一件紫色装备附带4个"词条"只有1条NB,那就是4分之1的几率才能得到,那凑够3条NB属性我要刷多久?假设一趟"我有修改系统之重生"我玩2小时一局,我会用1小时刷属性做装备吗(1小时根本不够,还得刷矿产呢)?辛苦做完装备一重生全清空那我图啥??就是让玩家,所有天赋点满通关后,在用这个系统吗? (以下脚本为DeepSeek生成) @echo off :: 增加1小时 powershell -Command "Set-Date -Adjust (New-TimeSpan -Hours 1)" :: 恢复时间（减少1小时） powershell -Command "Set-Date -Adjust (New-TimeSpan -Hours -1)" exit
天赋级别3以后数值开始极速膨胀，一个轮回就可以刷满天赋，点满天赋后一个轮回就可以变赛亚人，新开的轮回开局没多久，护甲就一千多万了，没发现游戏后续的挑战和玩下去的意义。前期强行让人轮回反复打剧情拖时间，最后也才十多个小时，游戏就几乎变成了无意义的数值爆炸。一坨答辩当之无愧。

Nothing says fun like being forced to reset your progress multiple times in order to access the next tier of empowerment. There's an overabundance of half-baked game systems and the central mechanic itself is nowhere near as deep as advertised: rewriting doesn't meaningfully alter your playstyle, the weapons, or build strategy. On my sixth go-around I finally decided that, no, I don't want to replay the threadbare campaign yet again just to eke out another incremental power bump. There are far more interesting Roguelites out there, some of which will even respect your time.
改写的玩法很有创新，但游戏本身其他问题很大，瑕不掩瑜。强行过剧情拉长游戏时间，内容空洞，装备少，从头到尾只能用一艘船，纯数值游戏，无聊且重复。卖20我可能会给好评，卖50这就是个工业垃圾。
This game is like bread. I love bread, but this is only bread. No butter, no jam, no cheese, just... bread. Lot's of bread. The same bread. Bread: over and over. Bread for every meal.

It's a fun idea, but why make it a roguelike? Knowing my equipment will soon be just wiped out makes me care about it a lot less, and knowing my stash will be cleared out makes me not want to bother picking up crafting resources. It also makes going through the story incredibly annoying. Awesome basis for a game, but I personally wish they slowed it down a little and removed the roguelike aspects in favor of a different progression system.

It's not a bad game, but it's not worth the high asking price. The campaign is very short and only lasts as long as it does (a few hours at most) because there are several points where it unavoidably kills you and makes you do the whole thing over with maybe one or two different dialog lines. The game would be a lot more fun if the loot was better, but there is very little variety and doesn't appear to be any loot progression outside of the meta progression mechanic from restarting. There are only a scant few different weapon types and everything feels really under powered. Even some of the basic enemies take 100 hits to kill and then they drop items that are much worse than what you're using already. Since my latest restart, about an hour ago, I've found at least 200 items. Not a single one of these was better (stat wise) than the items I picked up from the first enemies I killed so there isn't really any point in picking them up. The worst part of this experience is my first couple runs didn't feel like this at all, so I wasn't expecting it to be this unrewarding in the later stages. It's also very buggy. About 3 of my 9 hours of playtime were spent trying to get around a game breaking bug in one of the missions that requires you to fly into an area that instantly kills you unless you have a special shield that just randomly stopped working for me. According to the forums, this is a rare bug that happens occasionally, but it happened to me in each of my 3 restarts and I've yet to find a way past it. The rewrite mechanic is neat, but you only get the opportunity to use it a few times outside of changing up the side missions you don't want to complete.

看了下价格，60的话，应该是个差评。这款游戏的实际价值应该在20~40左右。优点是作为一个刷子游戏，数值可以翻的够爽，然后似乎有无尽的难度可以挑战。 但缺点更致命： 1 作为刷子游戏，几个小时刷不出一件能用的东西。 （ 这也是最大的问题，刷子游戏刷不出东西。让其极度重复的玩法变得超级无聊。） 2 新鲜感大概也就只有3~10个小时，你能玩的内容基本前3个小时就看光90%了。 （其实要是能刷出装备，一层层的强化下去，换下去，还是爽的。但又不好玩，又不出东西，就恶心了。） 3 优化极差，导致很多套路玩不了。看着很爽：射速+1000%每次射击增加100个投射物，投射物打到敌人自动弹射附近的敌人5次，神器还自带1000%以上的分裂子弹。但——不用说你也能猜到吧，真打够肉的敌人，直接画面卡成PPT。导致只能玩些高乘算的装备堆纯数值。 4 成长曲线很烂，刷图的感觉就只有两种：摸一下就秒 和 疯狂刮痧卡成PPT，没有“成长过程”。 （ 我能玩30多个小时，因为全程就就差一个全身神器，然后刷了好久都没出。（早就点了全天赋，最大概率出稀有度改造。）好烦，不想玩了，但又刷不到。有点折磨了。）
无意义的轮回只让玩家痛苦，流程过短重复是大多数，标题界面十分帅气但实际上装备页面还不如最早的暗黑破坏神，装备只是图标，安装装备并不能使人感觉到飞船大的变化，武器过于单一，飞船升级的材料每轮回一次就要重复刷取。
我本来觉得玩的挺好，直到一次轮回后我费劲巴拉攒了那么多现实点出来，在局外成长里挑挑拣拣，最后手一抖右键了一下天赋，天赋没了，那么多点数不返还 制作组nmsbssl，这么关键的东西，右键一下就直接执行了，没有确认框，也没有大版面提示，就没了，在鼠标挪上去才给一行小逼字说资源不返还，不返还尼姆，不返还就该给很明确的提示锕，而且我也是第一次见会吞玩家局外成长资源的游戏，真78纽币

If you will complain about performance you will get a perma ban and your thread will be deleted. Performance is unacceptable, for what it visually is (basically isometric space shoot-em-up), it eats more resources than stunning full 3D environment games. Which leads me to believe that devs have no clue about compsci at all and have just mashed together default Unity modules and shipped it. Refunding because its not acceptable to ship this in its current state.

The main issue is the illusion of depth. I was consistently shown something seemingly interesting and then I was let down again and again. An easy example is that there are items in the game that suggest there are different ship types, "Capital Ship" and "Warship", they're bigger items, using the main gimmick of the game you can reduce their size to let them fit on your fighter ship and at first you get excited because you're taking different classes' abilities and mix matching them to make a fun build. Except, 16 hours in, there has been no mention of different ships you can pilot and the slow realisation that I will never get to pilot a different ship type is really demotivating. This kind of disappointment happens again and again, which is a shame because the idea is great and this is my type of game entirely. Another issue is performance, very quickly when there are supposedly many enemies the game gets incredibly choppy and it's unplayable, in a genre where many enemies is common and expected this really effects gameplay early on. The story is great, fun writing, I wish there were more options with the rewrite mechanic but it's mostly a funny and likeable part of the game.

EDIT 2: I got to the endgame, and I'll say there are elements that are definitely disappointing, which I hate to say about this game. It has a lot of neat build opportunities, loot is plentiful, the graphics are flashy and surprisingly beautiful, and this has some of the best feeling controls to a space shooter that I've seen in a while. Combat feels smooth, surprisingly cinematic at times, and is just a joy to look at. It has a LOT of good things going for it. Its biggest weakness is that it appears to have significant depth, yet struggles to deliver the content to achieve that depth. Much of the loot feels superfluous, and upon reaching the endgame, it felt very much like I had experienced almost everything the game has to offer. For an indie game produced by a single person, this is an EXTREMELY impressive effort, and has some absurdly complex systems that can lend to some really incredible builds and gameplay. But in the end, it's a space shooter where you fly about and shoot, and that's the primary combat mechanic. That's not to say that the game itself is not fun - anyone who likes a good schmup will find something to enjoy about this game. It just feels like it could be MORE, like it's SO close to breaking past its own limitations and being something truly ground-breaking. It needs some additional meaning to the loot, the build trees, the weapon variety, and even just a few more boosts to the combat mechanics would be amazing. This game is on the edge of something great, and just a little more can get it there. EDIT: Soooo I just found out this entire game has been produced by a solo dev. HOLY CRAP that changes my perspective further. Creating a game with this many complex systems by yourself is NOT easy, and the sheer level of undertaking necessary to achieve something like this is frankly staggering. Whatever the flaws of the game may be, the developer, Courtney, did it. She made the game she has dreamed of for years, and that alone is an achievement well worth applauding. Original Review: So, this one caught me off guard. At first, I was frankly unimpressed. The dialogue feels very bland and largely unecessary, the core gameplay loop seemed really limited at first, and there didn't seem to be enough variety to the loot, which is a problem for a looter shooter. It is listed as a roguelite, but I don't get very many roguelike elements to it - it's not permadeath EXCEPT for specific events that "break" your profile, effectively starting your playthrough over in a frankly odd mechanic designed to forward the story. This mechanic unfortunately forces you to replay the exact same events almost verbatim, dialogue and all, with only minor changes to dialogue as you progress. While that is a staple of roguelikes (same levels, specific bosses, randomized loot/upgrades, etc.), being able to die and respawn immediately without losing progress and re-experiencing identical story dialogue break parts of the roguelike experience for me (and the single largest category of games I own and play the most are roguelikes). It's got a fair few programming issues, with occasionally odd enemy movement (namely for the bigger battleships), and for a seemingly simple space shooter, the graphics and systems are not well-optimized to prevent framerate drops. Though I have an older geforce 1660 super, I can run games like Destiny 2 VERY comfortably, and even Monster Hunter World plays butter smooth on nearly max graphics. To see a game like this cause lower framerates is a little frustrating. Certain upgrades and loot feel unfortunately bland and unhelpful - afterburner seems to be the only consistently viable boost/dodge, with the others like teleport having a fairly long cooldown before you can dodge again. Much of the loot that you pick up feels frankly unhelpful and useless for anything but to sell for credits. HOWEVER..... The gameplay is amazing outside of these various complaints. What started out as limited loot became MUCH more exciting on the discovery of my first epic item. The affixes are so random that it is hard at first to synergize your builds, but the epic items are often so powerful that this fails to matter for long. The game has many systems you unlock that assist with addressing the various weaknesses of the game - even the low quality of the loot can be improved by finding loot that increases your "loot quality" percentages, and even a 15% increase in this stat drastically improves the items you get. As you further the story, a slew of upgrades become available that allow you to take already powerful items and add even MORE power to them. I'm only on my 3rd playthrough to progress the story, and I have gotten a whopping 5000+ armor (basically, I can't die much). Add an additional story upgrade that allows you to transfer affixes from existing items onto a brand new piece, and suddenly you have the ability to slowly create a customized, perfected build. The possibilities have already expanded wildly. Progressing the story seems to be the way to go to get not only better loot, but better build customization. On the occasions that your profile "breaks" due to a story event, you can unlock substantial, permanent upgrades that add a massive layer of survivability and tools to allow you to succeed where you struggled before. The graphics are delightfully crisp and beautiful. The title screen got me to oo and ah the first time I saw it. There is a wonderful joy and enjoyment to being able to boost around in your spaceship and blow stuff up. Despite its flaws and weaknesses, it's a different enough experience from a traditional roguelike to be a refreshing take on the genre, and the developer has shown interest in feedback, and expressed a desire to work on and improve the game further, so I am excited to see what else she comes up with. I have already enjoyed this game much more than I initially thought I would, and for that reason alone, I am quite pleased with my purchase and happy to play it further.

The game is well-made. After 70 hours of playtime, here’s my input: 1. More weapon variety – Add unique types to keep combat fresh. 2. Better endgame – Include more mission types (mining, racing, quick puzzles). Avoid long puzzles—players often dislike them. 3. Expanded skill tree – Limit some nodes to unlock new playstyles, not just maxing everything. 4. More weapon mods – Example: A laser mod splits beams into three but reduces damage by 30% per line. 5. Improved gear upgrades – Current crafted gear trivializes post-Challenge 40. Add fusion/enchantment systems. 6. Optimization fixes – FPS drops below 10 with high-end hardware (RTX 5080, 13th-gen CPU) during heavy projectile use.

优点: BD深度还是可以的 虽然独特装备数量略有不足 但是有不少联动效果 局外成长除了最后的升华部分要硬刷之外其他都能在合理的时间内完成，并且很有正反馈 缺点主要在于：做装系统和轮回事实上并不会很好的融合。 刷词条，刷独特可以看见需要大量投入，上限也很高。但是，单局的高强度并不会带来很多的局外收益。强度成多项式增长的同时，怪物的强度成指数级增长， 而混沌对现实点的加成是随怪物等级成一次/二次方的，意味增长强度的收益小于线性，甚至不如重开一局，更别说局外的巨大成长能够让RP收益（和你的强度）上升几个数量级。 可以看到喜好物品的设定试图解决这个问题，但喜好物品每次轮回都有概率不能继承，爽了，但没完全爽。 升华点甚至是现实点取对数，那我堆局内强度不如每局就找一套及格的史诗/神器然后快速轮回，在这种情况下局内的做装系统（词条部分）基本没有作用 唯一能逃脱不能继承的只有单词条（取下来再装上去），那这样玩独特的意义是什么。 总之，局内做装和局外轮回这两个系统现在以一个很变扭的方式放在一起 一些其他问题: 中文翻译不准确，最后一排被动的第一个是次要武器给25%暴击几率，切英文是正确的 有时多个改写在同一词条时会有奇怪的顺序问题，例如改变类型后数值仍然显示原类型，改变运算符后数值修改不变（我用这个搞出了 x700 护甲的词条） 升华每次点前三层天赋很烦，能不能直接保存配置

If you’ve ever wondered what Diablo would feel like if you swapped the loot-heavy dungeons for deep space and a twin-stick flight model, this is it. It’s a tight, satisfying Space ARPG that hits that "one more run" itch perfectly. Gameplay & Mechanics Combat: The dual-stick shooting feels responsive and fluid. It’s not just mindless spamming; the positioning matters, and the controller support is baked in well. Loot & Progression: It leans hard into the ARPG staples. You’re going to get showered with items, and the upgrading systems are deep enough to keep you tinkering with your ship’s build. Flow: This is a fantastic "side game." It’s easy to jump in for 20 minutes, blow up some ships, upgrade your gear, and hop back out. Steam Deck Performance (OLED) I played almost all of my 3.6 hours on the Deck. It’s a natural fit for the handheld, though there’s a small caveat: Framerate: Even at 800p, I wasn’t hitting a locked 90fps. It stayed north of 60fps consistently, so it’s smooth, but given the art style, you'd expect it to max out the OLED's refresh rate effortlessly. Visuals: Clean and functional. It won't melt your GPU, but it looks great on the smaller screen. Final Thoughts It’s a great pickup for anyone who wants an ARPG that trades swords for thrusters. If you're looking for a new "on-the-go" obsession for your Deck, this is a safe bet.

This game combines an ARPG with Roguelite permanent progression, and honestly, i wish i could only play the ARPG. The gameplay is plenty of fun, a space shmup does fantastic with all your ARPG gameplay staples. Loot galore with rarity filtering is a great touch. However, the game boils down to this: How many times can we block progression behind constantly looping back to the start to go through the same boring, soulless progression slowing dialogue (even when skipping), just so you have an opportunity to get the same loot, with minimal upgrades to go up against spongier and spongier enemies? all so you can do the same thing again. and mind you, you'll probably only get about 5-10 minutes forward in your progression before you need to start all over again. No variety in your gameplay and no justification for having to constantly loop back. having 1 little item that is pivotal to the story and holds the entirety of this mechanic together is one of the most laughable things i've ever witnessed in gaming. i don't see a good fix that satisfies this. obviously, this is what the game has been built around. this IS the vision. if that's the case, i recommend other ARPGS or roguelikes on their own instead of this failed amalgamation.

As a lover of ARPGs, especially the shmuppy sort, I have found my home for the next good little while. The storyline isn't super-long, but it's got some good punches along the way. The controls and gameplay are pretty tight. You absolutely will not lack for loot to enjoy -- thankfully there is a highly-configurable loot filter available by the time mountains of loot start to become an issue. The several methods of upgrading items open up all sorts of possibilities for ship loadouts. Weapons are punchy and fun, with some excellent sound design for both player and enemy vessels. The sound and visuals for elite ships exploding might be one of the best dopamine hits I've had in a while from any game, especially when it's a whole bunch of 'em! The meta-progression is handled really well. I don't want to say too much, because spoilers suck, but I'm enjoying it enough that I plan to see it through to the end. Thanks so much for making this gem of a game -- your love for what you did here shines through pretty much everywhere and I have delighted in discovering every moment of it.

Games in this style have a balance between your character's strength being equipment based and skill based. Too skill based and the player has no upgrade path. Too equipment based and the game just feels like a grind. If 5 were balanced in the middle, this game would be an 8 or a 9 towards equipment based. There are too many enemy shots, and your dodge ability has a cooldown, so you can't dodge everything and aiming is mostly just putting the mouse near the enemy. There is skill, it just doesn't have anywhere near the impact of your equipment. So the game is grindy, but oddly the storyline forces you to reset your character and lose all equipment in order to progress farther. Another problem is the game doesn't explain very well what the stats and modifiers on equipment do. So my inventory would fill up fast but I wouldn't really know what was better or not and it was hard to tell what synergized or not. Just went by if it had a green indicator and if the price was higher. You can basically pay to upgrade gear, but again I don't know why I'd bother with that since my character will reset soon anyway. All in all after 2 hours I felt bored and annoyed and didn't want to play anymore.

It's like diablo in space, minus skill trees and build making and focused mostly on gear. The twist is that reality "breaks" at scripted points of the story, deleting your character and giving you the ability to repeat the thing by "changing reality" at that point next time you reach it (there is no puzzle there, it's literally a dialogue option saying "change reality"). Maybe it gets more interesting later, but the first 2 times you really are just killed without ceremony and forced to restart. Sure, doing this gives you the chance to get permanent upgrades by spending "reality points" and the story moves faster (you have some skip options) the second time, but it still undoes part of the grinder for no real reason. The game looks okay, not amazing. Performance suffers in busier levels. Ultimately, it's a numbers game. If you're underleveled, enemies are absolute sponges and melt you with unavoidable attacks; if you're overleveled, you melt them and are largely impervious to their attacks. Combat is generally fun and it's satisfying to see numbers go up, but... why? There's no real reason for me to play this, and the story so far has presented neither interest nor agency. It's just an excuse to shoot things. But it's not like Escape Velocity where trading and upgrading your ship is part of your thought process - instead, you just go on random missions and get random loot, replacing your equipment when RNG rewards you with something better. There has been no world building outside the very on-rails story, either. Maybe it opens up and gets better later on, but I don't really want to stick around to find out.

This game wants to be better than it is. Unfortunately it suffers from memory leaks, poor optimizations, and the in-game stated goal of "becoming overpowered" is hampered by the program itself being unable to handle pursuing that. The writing is good, which makes it ironic that it's the only easily skippable thing. The graphics are okay, too much bloom and LoD and the map is obnoxious to use regardless of settings. The grind to upgrade things is painful and slow, and it becomes a chore. My playtime is inflated from leaving the game running to preserve "mission flow combos" which are lost any time you close the program. I feel I eventually got my money's worth after wringing the towel bone dry, but I don't recommend picking this up new for anyone.
